Field notes 08 · 5 August 2026

Fear enters the room before he does

A leader who is none of the bad bosses, and a team that has learned to say as little as possible.

A short mail from head office lands on the desk of the site leader: why is the programme late? He does not know. He is certain his team does.

His office door stays open all day. At lunch he takes his tray to whichever table has a free chair. He is proud of that. He began his career on this site. He remembers bosses that everyone was afraid of, and he knows he is not one of them.

He does not just forward the mail from head office. He adds two lines of his own, harder than anything they wrote: “This cannot wait. I need answers today.” He is not accusing anyone. He is trying to get the thing done. It arrives as an accusation anyway. One of his engineers replies before lunch, and everything in her reply is true: her work was finished on time. It is waiting for lab time at another site, and the queue is two months long. The other answers are true in the same way. Each covers one piece of the programme, and together they still do not answer the question. No one is lying. No one is hiding anything. The mail sits in his stomach all day. To the team, it is just another urgent mail.

The real answer is months old. When the plan was made, nobody checked the lab queue. Nobody decided to work blind. Checking another team's queue feels like stepping into their territory, and that has a price everyone knows.

His people are independent experts. They know their work better than he does, so he stays out of their way and calls it respect. It also means a warning can reach him only one way: someone walks into his office and says it to his face. And before anyone does that, they read his mood first.

He calls a meeting for two o'clock and hears his own voice getting sharper. The room gets quieter as he gets louder. He reads the silence as proof they still do not understand.

When I am called in, months later, both stories have hardened: a leader who cannot rely on his team, and a team that has learned to say as little as possible. The programme pays for both. By then, fear enters the room before he does.

There is a test. Think of the last person who told you about a problem while it was still small. What happened to them next? If no one comes to mind, that is also an answer.

Anna Chodynicka, DRIFT Partners · First published on LinkedIn, 5 August 2026
